npcs.name: Miller Oswin
dialogue: Millhaven's mill has ground grain for this coast for sixty years.
Three grain sacks went missing from the store. Someone's been helping themselves.
If you find those sacks, I'll remember the favour.

npcs.name: Fishwife Marta
dialogue: The catch has been thin lately. Strange currents, says Sailor Finn.
I've got fish baskets missing somewhere around the docks.
Fresh catch, get your fresh catch! Don't let the gulls beat you to it.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Cobb
dialogue: Welcome to The Anchor, best beds on the Millhaven coast.
A merchant from Ravenwatch left a letter here. Meant for someone called Elder Elara.
You look like someone who travels. That letter's been sitting here long enough.

npcs.name: Elder Bramwell
dialogue: Millhaven was founded by fisherfolk. We've kept it that way.
The castle to the south needs resupply. We've been meaning to send a courier.
If you're heading to Ironhold Keep, perhaps you could take our supply manifest to Commander Varek?

npcs.name: Sailor Finn
dialogue: The tides have been off all week. Something in the currents.
I've seen three ships go dark past the reef. No word from them.
Marta thinks I'm superstitious. Maybe I am.

npcs.name: Trader Nessa
dialogue: Everything from rope to ribbon, if you've got coin.
Trade's been slow. Travellers don't stop here like they used to.
Nice to see a fresh face in Millhaven.

npcs.name: Baker Pernel
dialogue: Fresh loaves out of the oven — mind, they're still warm.
Half the town runs on my bread and the other half on Marta's fish.
If you're passing the docks, folk down there are always after a delivery.

npcs.name: Smith Garrick
dialogue: Mind the sparks. Forge runs hot this time of day.
Net hooks, anchor chain, blades — if it's iron, I've hammered it.
Scrap's been going missing from my yard. A smith can't work without iron.

npcs.name: Dockhand Bram
dialogue: Careful on the boards, they're slick with spray.
Storm last week dragged half our nets out past the moorings.
The boathouse keeps the town's boats — and most of its gossip.

npcs.name: Widow Tamsin
dialogue: Forgive the mess. It's just me in this little cottage now.
I lost my late husband's locket somewhere out in the town. It's all I have of him.
You have a kind face. Perhaps you'd keep an eye out for it?

npcs.name: Old Pellan
dialogue: Best fishing on the coast, right off this dock.
Cast a line with me — the harbour's always biting.
Patience and a steady hand, that's all it takes.

npcs.name: Quartermaster Hale
dialogue: Potions, provisions, the lot — stocked fresh off the boats.
A traveller far from home still needs to resupply. Take a look.
Coin for goods, that's the honest trade of Millhaven.

npcs.name: Dealer Sloane
dialogue: Cards! Rare cards, off the trade ships and into your deck.
No need to trek back to Ravenwatch — I deal right here.
Browse the wares, friend. Every deck needs an edge.

npcs.name: Regatta Master Coll
dialogue: One day Millhaven will host a proper boat regatta — skiffs racing the harbour buoys, crowds on the quay!
Rigging's done and the buoys are set — care to race a skiff?
Mark my words: the Millhaven Regatta will be the finest sport on the coast.

reactions.text: A tangled bush growing wild by the fisher-cottage field.
A shaded bush behind the bakery, worth a closer look.
A patch of wildflowers growing at the field's edge.
Tucked beneath the fishmonger's awning, a small carved charm has been wedged into a support post for years.

collectible.name: Weathered Sailor's Charm
collectible.desc: A small wooden charm, carved in the shape of an anchor.
collectible.lore: Sailor Finn would recognize the carving style — sailors used to nail these to the post before a long haul. Whoever left this one never came back to reclaim it.

reactions.message: You found a weathered sailor's charm.

reactions.text: Half-tangled in old netting near the tackle stalls, a small buoy bobs against the pilings.

collectible.name: Faded Marker Buoy
collectible.desc: A small buoy, its paint faded past recognition.
collectible.lore: Dockhand Bram mentioned the storm dragged half the moorings loose last week. This one never made it back to its post.

reactions.message: You found a faded marker buoy tangled in the nets.

reactions.text: Wedged behind the smithy's log pile, a small hand tool has rusted into the wood.

collectible.name: Rusted Forge Tool
collectible.desc: A small hand tool, its handle long rotted away.
collectible.lore: Smith Garrick would swear he's never lost a tool in his life. This one's older than his apprenticeship, by the rust on it.

reactions.message: You found a rusted old forge tool.

reactions.text: Behind the storm-blown crate the buoy seemed to be marking, a small chest sits half-buried in the mud.

collectible.name: Storm-Washed Cache
collectible.desc: A small chest, salt-stained and swollen from the rain.
collectible.lore: Whatever ship it fell from, the tide brought it all the way into the square. Regatta Master Coll would probably want to hear about this.

reactions.message: You found a storm-washed cache in the square!
